diagnosis.root_cause: Two active CRM records are assigned to the same physical ONU slot EPON0/4:17, for line IDs 4C:D7:C8:93:BA:F1 and 4C:D7:C8:7F:0A:B9. Only one ONU can legitimately occupy that slot, indicating a provisioning or inventory collision.
evidence: The live ONU probe responds and reports online, with normal RX power of -20.91 dBm and TX power of 2.38 dBm.
The seven-day RX and TX telemetry is stable, distance remains constant at 134, and TX bias current remains within the healthy range, so there is no evidence of fibre, laser, or distance fault.
All tested peers on EPON0/4 are online, so there is no shared PON, splitter, or OLT outage.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, has healthy CPU, memory, and temperature, and the router heartbeat is healthy.
The subscriber has only two sessions in 24 hours with approximately normal duration, so there is no session flapping.
RADIUS data is present and CRM-consistent, and the expected customer VLAN 1044 is active, so there is no authentication or VLAN fault.
The explicit duplicate_slot_conflict identifies two active CRM records on the same physical slot EPON0/4:17; this direct configuration conflict is the fault.

remediation.action: Verify the physical ONU MAC/serial currently occupying EPON0/4:17, reconcile it with the subscriber and CRM records, remove or correct the stale duplicate assignment, and reprovision the affected customer record if necessary. Recheck the slot and both customer services after the correction.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two active CRM records place different ONU MACs on EPON0/4:17. A slot holds exactly one ONU, so one record is stale. The live probe returns a single device, and its MAC matches the subject record, identifying the other as the leftover.
expected_reasoning: The CRM view lists two active customers on EPON0/4:17 with different ONU MACs
A PON slot holds exactly one ONU, so this state is physically impossible
The live probe of that slot returns a single responding device
The probe's optical values match the subject record's cached reading of -20.88 dBm
RADIUS holds a consistent entry for the subject with normal sessions and traffic
The second record therefore does not correspond to an installed device and is stale
The optical layer is healthy and neither customer is experiencing a service fault
This is a record defect of the same class as the 644 such interfaces in the estate

expected_escalation.review_reason: One of two CRM records on this slot is stale; deleting the wrong one disconnects a live customer

distractors: Nothing is failing and no customer has complained
Both records are marked active and look equally legitimate in CRM
